name: Cursor
soft_passes: #4 16px squint — the hexagonal cube outline survives and is nameable as 'a cube', but the two mid-dark facets (#43 vs #55, ~1.2:1 apart) merge and the bright-blade cursor dual-reading smears out; at menu-bar size it's a generic gray cube with its wit dropped (structural: achromatic + low internal contrast on the dark faces, aggravated by 204px source)

#2 grid adherence estimated only — optical centring and safe-zone margins look right and the cube sits marginally high (correct optical bias), but the true Apple grid can't be overlaid on a 204px render
#3 silhouette borderline — filled solid black the mark is a clean hexagon nameable as 'a cube', but the cursor half of the concept lives entirely in the tonal facets and vanishes in pure silhouette
failures: #10 variant robustness (Liquid Glass) — composition is defined against a baked near-black tile: the dark cube facets (#43413D) read only because the ground is darker still; on a clear/tinted/light render the opaque tile can't take system tint and, if the ground lightens, the dark back-faces lose figure-ground and the cube collapses toward a flat white silhouette; the icon does not participate in the current era's material system

palette.background: flat #13120B (warm olive-tinted near-black, truly flat — no ramp/vignette)

light_model: Object-internal directional light from upper-front-left: top face and central blade brightest, side faces progressively darker, back-right face darkest. Flat faceted vector shading — NO cast shadow on the tile, no ambient occlusion, no specular/glass. Coherent on the object, but self-lit brand illustration, not Big Sur baked-micro-shadow nor Liquid Glass environmental light.
devices: dual-read cube-cursor — the bright inverted triangle reads simultaneously as the cube's near vertical edge/front facet AND as a downward-pointing cursor/pointer blade; one geometric move carries both '3D agent/environment' and 'cursor'
tonal ramp as self-lighting with zero hue — a monochrome facet ramp (#43->#55->#D9->#FFF) does all the 3D work, the opposite pole from the LLM-era violet->blue glass blob
vanishing back-faces — darkest facets (#43413D) sit ~1.5:1 against the #13120B tile so the cube's far edges melt into the ground and it reads open/floating, letting the bright blade dominate
rhymes_hint: Achromatic dev/AI-tool logo-on-near-black tiles (company glyph dropped on a flat dark square); isometric-cube brand marks (cube = environment/package/build); the cross-platform/Electron flat brand-tile pattern. Style family: flat faceted brand-mark on flat dark tile, achromatic, no system-material participation. Notably the inverse route to Codex, which answers the same 'AI coding agent' brief with a light ground + saturated indigo glass.
notes: Source icon is a 204x204 webp resized web render, NOT the 1024 master — all px/positional reads (estimated); hex values reliable at facet centres, edges anti-aliased. Pixels outside the squircle flatten to #FFFFFF, so the source is a PRE-MASKED squircle PNG (cross-platform/Electron brand tile), not an unmasked full-bleed layer for the system to mask — mask discipline (#1) inferred clean rather than measured, and this is itself the tell for era='custom'. Background is genuinely flat (9 samples identical) — the halo seen on upscale is a NEAREST artifact. Cursor is a VS Code fork (Electron), so this is the company's cross-platform monochrome logo on a dark tile, not an AppKit-native Icon Composer composition; that's why it neither uses Big Sur soft top-down baked shadow nor Liquid Glass layer/specular/translucency. Cover art (near-black field, white 'CURSOR' geometric-sans wordmark + the same cube) confirms deliberate achromatic brand coherence icon<->brand. Strong data point for a 'flat achromatic logo-on-dark-tile' device family and a direct contrast pair with codex-icon for the AI-coding-tool cluster.
